units.en: From boyhood he carried himself like his uncle Xiahou Xuan—aloof and exacting.
units.literal: Jiao from youth had bearing—admired maternal uncle Xiahou Xuan’s person—greatly esteemed himself.

units.zh: 有盛名于世，朝野許其能風俗，理人倫。
units.en: Court and countryside praised him for shaping manners and moral order.
units.literal: He had great fame in the world—court and wild approved his ability to move custom and order human relations.

units.zh: 襲父爵上蔡伯，起家太子舍人。
units.en: He succeeded the barony of Shangcai and entered service as heir‑apparent attendant.
units.literal: Inherited father’s noble rank Baron of Shangcai—first office heir-apparent attendant.

units.zh: 累遷潁川太守，為政清簡，甚得百姓歡心。
units.en: As Yingchuan prefect he ruled plainly and won the people.
units.literal: Promoted repeatedly to prefect of Yingchuan—administration clear and simple—greatly won common people’s hearts.

units.zh: 太傅從事中郎庾敳見而歎曰：「嶠森森如千丈松，雖磥砢有節目，施之大廈，有棟樑之用。」
units.en: Yu Ai marveled: "He Jiao is a thousand-foot pine—rough bark and all—yet palace timber."
units.literal: Adjutant to the grand tutor Yu Ai saw him and sighed: "Jiao stands tall like a thousand-foot pine—though gnarled and knotty—applied to a great hall—has timber-and-beam use."

units.zh: 賈充亦重之，稱于武帝，入為給事黃門侍郎，遷中書令，帝深器遇之。
units.en: Jia Chong praised him to the throne; he entered the palace secretariat and became an imperial favorite.
units.literal: Jia Chong also esteemed him—praised him to Emperor Wu—entered as gentleman attendant at the yellow gate—promoted director of the palace secretariat—Emperor deeply prized him.

units.zh: 舊監令共車入朝，時荀勖為監，嶠鄙勖為人，以意氣加之，每同乘，高抗專車而坐。
units.en: Overseer and director once rode together; Jiao scorned Xun Xu and insisted on a separate cart.
units.literal: By old practice overseer and director shared carriage into court—at time Xun Xu was overseer—Jiao despised Xu’s person—applied spirit of pride—each time riding together—held head high and sat exclusive carriage.

units.zh: 乃使監令異車，自嶠始也。
units.en: Separate carts for overseer and director began with He Jiao.
units.literal: Thereupon made overseer and director different carriages—beginning with Jiao.

units.zh: 吳平，以參謀議功，賜弟郁爵汝南亭侯。
units.en: After Wu was pacified, for He Jiao’s merit in planning counsel his younger brother Yu was granted the rank of Marquis of Runan Pavilion.
units.literal: When Wu was pacified—for planning merit—granted younger brother Yu noble rank Marquis of Runan Pavilion.

units.zh: 嶠轉侍中，愈被親禮，與任愷、張華相善。
units.en: As palace attendant he grew closer to the throne and befriended Ren Kai and Zhang Hua.
units.literal: Jiao transferred to palace attendant—more favored—in friendship with Ren Kai and Zhang Hua.

units.zh: 嶠見太子不令，因侍坐曰：「皇太子有淳古之風，而季世多偽，恐不了陛下家事。」
units.en: At leisure he said: "The crown prince has an antique plainness, yet a decadent age breeds sham—I fear he cannot manage Your Majesty's household."
units.literal: Jiao seeing heir apparent was not sound—therefore sitting attendance said: "Crown prince has pure antique manner—but declining age abounds in sham—fears he cannot manage Your Majesty’s household affairs."

units.zh: 帝默然不答。
units.en: The emperor stayed silent.
units.literal: Emperor silent—did not answer.

units.zh: 後與荀顗、荀勖同侍，帝曰：「太子近入朝，差長進，卿可俱詣之，粗及世事。」
units.en: Later, with the Xuns attending, the emperor said: "The heir has lately entered court and made some progress—you may all visit him and touch on affairs of state."
units.literal: Later together attending with Xun Yi and Xun Xu—Emperor said: "Heir apparent lately entered court—somewhat grown—you may all visit him—roughly touch on worldly affairs."

units.zh: 即奉詔而還。
units.en: They bowed and withdrew.
units.literal: Immediately obeyed edict and returned.

units.zh: 顗、勖並稱太子明識弘雅，誠如明詔。
units.en: Xun Yi and Xun Xu flattered the prince’s polish.
units.literal: Yi and Xu together praised heir apparent’s bright understanding—vast and refined—truly as enlightened edict.

units.zh: 嶠曰：「聖質如初耳！」
units.en: He Jiao said: "His sagely substance is just as before!"
units.literal: Jiao said: "Sagely substance like first!"

units.zh: 帝不悅而起。
units.en: The emperor rose in anger.
units.literal: Emperor displeased—rose.

units.zh: 嶠退居，恆懷慨歎，知不見用，猶不能已。
units.en: He brooded—knowing his counsel spurned yet unable to stay mute.
units.literal: Jiao withdrew—always harbored sighing regret—knew not employed—still could not stop.

units.zh: 在御坐言及社稷，未嘗不以儲君為憂。
units.en: Whenever talk touched the realm’s fate he fretted over the heir.
units.literal: On imperial seat speaking of altars of soil and grain—never without taking heir as worry.

units.zh: 帝知其言忠，每不酬和。
units.en: The emperor knew him faithful yet refused to engage.
units.literal: Emperor knew his words loyal—each time did not respond in harmony.

units.zh: 後與嶠語，不及來事。
units.en: Later audiences skirted the succession entirely.
units.literal: Later speaking with Jiao—did not reach future matters.

units.zh: 或以告賈妃，妃銜之。
units.en: Word reached Empress Jia—she nursed a grudge.
units.literal: Someone informed Consort Jia—consort bore grudge.

units.zh: 太康末，為尚書，以母憂去職。
units.en: Late in Taikang he headed the ministry until mourning his mother.
units.literal: Late Taikang—became minister of state affairs—left office for mother’s mourning.

units.zh: 及惠帝即位，拜太子少傅，加散騎常侍、光祿大夫。
units.en: Under Emperor Hui he tutored the crown prince with added honorifics.
units.literal: When Emperor Hui mounted throne—appointed junior tutor to heir—added regular attendant at casual riding and grand messenger at court.

units.zh: 太子朝西宮，嶠從入。
units.en: He accompanied the heir to the western palace.
units.literal: Heir apparent attended western palace—Jiao followed within.

units.zh: 賈后使帝問嶠曰：「卿昔謂我不了家事，今日定云何？」
units.en: The empress had the emperor ask him: "You once said I could not manage the household—what is your judgment today?"
units.literal: Empress Jia had Emperor ask Jiao: "You once said I could not manage household affairs—today settled how?"

units.zh: 嶠曰：「臣昔事先帝，曾有斯言。
units.en: He Jiao said: "Your servant once served the late emperor and spoke this warning.
units.literal: Jiao said: "Your servant formerly served late Emperor—once had this saying.

units.zh: 言之不效，國之福也。
units.en: That it proved false was the realm’s luck.
units.literal: Words not fulfilled—state’s fortune.

units.zh: 臣敢逃其罪乎！」
units.en: How dare your servant flee the blame!"
units.literal: Your servant dare flee the blame!"

units.zh: 元康二年卒，贈金紫光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，本位如前。
units.en: He died in Yuankang 2 and was posthumously honored as Grandee of Splendid Happiness with Gold and Purple, with gold seal and purple sash, his original rank unchanged.
units.literal: He died in Yuankang 2; he was posthumously granted Grandee of Splendid Happiness with Gold and Purple, with gold seal and purple ribbon added, while his original rank remained as before.

units.zh: 永平初，策諡曰簡。
units.en: Early Yongping era he was canonized “Jian.”
units.literal: Early Yongping—canon posthumous title Jian.

units.zh: 嶠家產豐富，擬于王者，然性至吝，以是獲譏于世，杜預以為嶠有錢癖。
units.en: He rivaled princes in wealth yet was famously stingy—Du Yu called it coin‑counting mania.
units.literal: Jiao household property rich—rivaling kings—yet nature utmost stingy—thereby earned ridicule in the world—Du Yu thought Jiao had money mania.

units.zh: 以弟郁子濟嗣，位至中書郎。
units.en: He adopted nephew Ji who rose to the secretariat.
units.literal: Younger brother Yu’s son Ji succeeded—rank reached gentleman of the palace secretariat.

units.zh: 弟郁
units.en: His brother He Yu
units.literal: Younger brother Yu

units.zh: =郁字仲輿，才望不及嶠，而以清幹稱，歷尚書左右僕射、中書令、尚書令。
units.en: He Yu, styled Zhongyu, was leaner in fame than He Jiao but famed for efficiency—he rose to chief minister posts.
units.literal: =Yu courtesy name Zhongyu—talent and reputation did not match Jiao—but by clarity and efficiency praised—served vice director left and right of the ministry—director of palace secretariat—minister of state affairs.

units.zh: 洛陽傾沒，奔于苟晞，疾卒。
units.en: When Luoyang fell he fled to Gou Xi and died sick.
units.literal: Luoyang collapsed—fled to Gou Xi—died of illness.

units.zh: 武陔
units.en: Wu Gai
units.literal: Wu Gai

units.zh: 武陔，字元夏，沛國竹邑人也。
units.en: Wu Gai, styled Yuanxia, came from Zhuyi in Pei commandery.
units.literal: Wu Gai, courtesy name Yuanxia, was a native of Zhuyi in Pei.

units.zh: 父周，魏衛尉。
units.en: His father Wu Zhou was Wei captain of the guards.
units.literal: Father Zhou—Wei captain of the guards.

units.zh: 陔沈敏有器量，早獲時譽，與二弟韶叔夏、茂季夏並總角知名，雖諸父兄弟及鄉閭宿望，莫能覺其優劣。
units.en: With brothers Shao and Mao he was celebrated since boyhood—even elders could not rank them.
units.literal: Gai deep and keen with vessel capacity—early gained timely praise—with two younger brothers Shao Shuxia and Mao Jixia together known from hair-tied youth—though uncles, brothers, and village elders of long standing—none could perceive their better or worse.

units.zh: 同郡劉公榮有知人之鑒，常造周，周見其三子焉。
units.en: Liu Gongrong of his county visited their father to judge the boys.
units.literal: Same commandery Liu Gongrong had mirror for knowing men—often visited Zhou—Zhou showed him his three sons.

units.zh: 公榮曰：「皆國士也。
units.en: Liu said: "All three are men of the state.
units.literal: Gongrong said: "All are men of the state.

units.zh: 元夏最優，有輔佐之才，陳力就列，可為亞公。
units.en: Yuanxia topped them—ministerial timber next to the Three Dukes.
units.literal: Yuanxia finest—has aide talent—deploying strength in rank—can be deputy to duke.

units.zh: 叔夏、季夏不減常伯、納言也。」
units.en: The younger two matched senior ministers."
units.literal: Shuxia and Jixia not inferior to ordinary grandee or spokesman."

units.zh: 陔少好人倫，與潁川陳泰友善。
units.en: Wu Gai loved appraising talent and befriended Chen Tai.
units.literal: Gai from youth loved ordering human relations—with Yingchuan Chen Tai friendly.

units.zh: 魏明帝世，累遷下邳太守。
units.en: Under Wei Mingdi he rose to Xiapi prefect.
units.literal: In Emperor Ming of Wei’s age—promoted repeatedly to prefect of Xiapi.

units.zh: 景帝為大將軍，引為從事中郎，累遷司隸校尉，轉太僕卿。
units.en: Prince Jing made him adjutant; he became metropolitan governor then minister of the imperial stud.
units.literal: Prince Jing as grand general—summoned as adjutant—promoted repeatedly metropolitan governor—transferred minister of the imperial stud.

units.zh: 初封亭侯，五等建，改封薛縣侯。
units.en: First a pavilion lord, he became marquis of Xue under the new rank system.
units.literal: First enfeoffed pavilion marquis—five ranks established—changed enfeoffment marquis of Xue county.

units.zh: 文帝甚親重之，數與詮論時人。
units.en: Emperor Wen cherished him and debated character with him often.
units.literal: Emperor Wen deeply favored him—often debated men of the time.

units.zh: 嘗問陳泰孰若其父群，陔各稱其所長，以為群、泰略無優劣，帝然之。
units.en: Asked to compare Chen Tai to Chen Qun, Wu Gai praised both equally—Wen agreed.
units.literal: Once asked Chen Tai compared to his father Qun—Gai praised each’s strengths—held Qun and Tai roughly without better or worse—Emperor assented.

units.zh: 泰始初，拜尚書，掌吏部，遷左僕射、左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。
units.en: Early Taishi he ran personnel, rose to vice director, grand messenger, and Three Offices parity.
units.literal: Taishi beginning—appointed minister of state affairs—presiding personnel—promoted vice director left—left grand messenger at court—opening office parity with Three Offices.

units.zh: 陔以宿齒舊臣，名位隆重，自以無佐命之功，又在魏已為大臣，不得已而居位，深懷遜讓，終始全潔，當世以為美談。
units.en: An elder statesman without founding laurels, he stayed humble in Wei-Jin transition—admired for unstained dignity.
units.literal: Gai as elder veteran minister—name and position weighty—himself thinking no merit aiding founding—and already great minister in Wei—had no choice but occupy post—deeply harbored yielding humility—beginning to end whole pure—contemporaries took as fine tale.

units.zh: 卒於位，諡曰定。
units.en: He died in office as “Ding.”
units.literal: Died in post—posthumous title Ding.

units.zh: 子輔嗣。
units.en: His son Wu Fu inherited.
units.literal: Son Fu succeeded.

units.zh: 弟韶
units.en: His brother Wu Shao
units.literal: Younger brother Shao

units.zh: =韶歷吏部郎、太子右衛率、散騎常侍。
units.en: Wu Shao rose through personnel, heir guard colonel, and attendant posts.
units.literal: =Shao served minister of personnel gentleman—colonel right guard of heir—regular attendant at casual riding.

units.zh: 弟茂
units.en: His brother Wu Mao
units.literal: Younger brother Mao

units.zh: =茂以德素稱，名亞於陔，為上洛太守、散騎常侍、侍中、尚書。
units.en: Wu Mao, famed for plain virtue just below Wu Gai, governed Shangluo and reached the ministries.
units.literal: =Mao by plain virtue praised—name second to Gai—prefect of Shangluo—regular attendant at casual riding—attendant-in-ordinary—minister of state affairs.

units.zh: 潁川荀愷年少於茂，即武帝姑子，自負貴戚，欲與茂交，距而不答，由是致怨。
units.en: Xun Kai of Yingchuan, younger than Mao and a son of Emperor Wu’s paternal aunt, prided himself on noble kinship, wished to befriend Mao, was refused, and therefore resented him.
units.literal: Yingchuan Xun Kai younger than Mao—being Emperor Wu’s cousin by aunt—self-important as noble kin—wished befriend Mao—refused distance—thereby incurred resentment.

units.zh: 及楊駿誅，愷時為僕射，以茂駿之姨弟，陷為逆黨，遂見害。
units.en: After Yang Jun fell, Xun Kai framed Wu Mao as Jun’s kin and had him killed.
units.literal: When Yang Jun executed—Kai then vice director—because Mao Jun’s maternal nephew—trapped as rebel clique—thereupon harmed.

units.zh: 茂清正方直，聞於朝野，一旦枉酷，天下傷焉。
units.en: Wu Mao’s wrongful death shocked the realm.
units.literal: Mao pure upright square straight—heard at court and wild—one morning twisted cruelty—world mourned.

units.zh: 侍中傅祗上申明之，後追贈光祿勳。
units.en: Fu Zhi cleared his name and won posthumous honors.
units.literal: Attendant Fu Zhi upward clarified—later posthumously gifted superintendent of the household.

units.zh: 任愷
units.en: Ren Kai
units.literal: Ren Kai

units.zh: 任愷，字元褒，樂安博昌人也。
units.en: Ren Kai, styled Yuanbao, came from Bochang in Le’an.
units.literal: Ren Kai, courtesy name Yuanbao, was a native of Bochang in Le’an.

units.zh: 父昊，魏太常。
units.en: His father Ren Hao was Wei minister of ceremonies.
units.literal: Father Hao—Wei minister of ceremonies.

units.zh: 愷少有識量，尚魏明帝女，累遷中書侍郎、員外散騎常侍。
units.en: He married a Wei princess and rose through secretariat and attendant posts.
units.literal: Kai from youth had judgment and capacity—married Emperor Ming of Wei’s daughter—promoted repeatedly gentleman of the palace secretariat—supernumerary regular attendant at casual riding.

units.zh: 晉國建，為侍中，封昌國縣侯。
units.en: When Jin was founded he became palace attendant and marquis of Changguo.
units.literal: When Jin state founded—palace attendant—enfeoffed marquis of Changguo county.

units.zh: 愷有經國之幹，萬機大小多管綜之。
units.en: He mastered statecraft large and small.
units.literal: Kai had capacity for ordering the state—myriad threads small and large mostly managed comprehensively.

units.zh: 性忠正，以社稷為己任，帝器而昵之，政事多諮焉。
units.en: Loyal and upright, he took the altars of the state as his own charge; the emperor prized and favored him and consulted him on most government affairs.
units.literal: Nature loyal upright—took altars of soil and grain as self-task—Emperor prized and favored—state affairs mostly consulted.

units.zh: 泰始初，鄭沖、王祥、何曾、荀顗、裴秀等各以老疾歸第。
units.en: Early Taishi the elder ministers retired ill.
units.literal: Taishi beginning—Zheng Chong—Wang Xiang—He Zeng—Xun Yi—Pei Xiu each by old age illness returned mansion.

units.zh: 帝優寵大臣，不欲勞以筋力，數遣愷諭旨于諸公，諮以當世大政，參議得失。
units.en: Wu sent Ren Kai to relay policy to the retired elders.
units.literal: Emperor graciously favored great ministers—did not wish labor them with sinews—often sent Kai conveying intent to each lord—consulting on age’s great policies—debating gain and loss.

units.zh: 愷惡賈充之為人也，不欲令久執朝政，每裁抑焉。
units.en: He worked to curb Jia Chong’s power.
units.literal: Kai hated Jia Chong’s person—did not wish him long hold court governance—each time restrained.

units.zh: 充病之，不知所為。
units.en: Jia Chong despaired.
units.literal: Chong sick at heart—knew not what to do.

units.zh: 後承間言愷忠貞局正，宜在東宮，使護太子。
units.en: He urged posting Ren Kai to tutor the heir—ostensibly praise.
units.literal: Later seizing interval spoke Kai loyal steadfast upright—ought be eastern palace—make protect heir.

units.zh: 帝從之，以為太子少傅，而侍中如故，充計畫不行。
units.en: The emperor followed and made him junior tutor to the heir, remaining palace attendant as before; Chong’s plan did not succeed.
units.literal: Emperor followed—thought junior tutor to heir—palace attendant as before—Chong’s plan did not proceed.

units.zh: 會秦、雍寇擾，天子以為憂。
units.en: Qinzhou and Yongzhou revolted—Wu fretted.
units.literal: When Qin and Yong raided and disturbed—Son of Heaven took as worry.

units.zh: 愷因曰：「秦、涼覆敗，關右騷動，此誠國家之所深慮。
units.en: Ren Kai said: "Qin and Liang have collapsed and the west is in turmoil—this truly is the state's deep worry.
units.literal: Kai therefore said: "Qin and Liang overturned defeated—right of Pass disturbed—this truly state’s deep worry.

units.zh: 宜速鎮撫，使人心有庇。
units.en: It needed a credible marshal to reassure the west.
units.literal: Ought quickly pacify soothe—make people’s hearts have shelter.

units.zh: 自非威望重臣有計略者，無以康西土也。」
units.en: Only a veteran minister of prestige and stratagem can pacify the western lands."
units.literal: Unless prestige-weighted minister with stratagem—none can heal western lands."

units.zh: 帝曰：「誰可任者？」
units.en: “Who fits?” asked the emperor.
units.literal: Emperor said: "Who can be appointed?"

units.zh: 愷曰：「賈充其人也。」
units.en: “Jia Chong,” said Ren Kai—setting a trap.
units.literal: Kai said: "Jia Chong is the man."

units.zh: 中書令庾純亦言之，於是詔充西鎮長安。
units.en: Yu Chun echoed the call—so Jia Chong was ordered west.
units.literal: Director of the palace secretariat Yu Chun also spoke—thereupon edict Chong west guard Chang’an.

units.zh: 充用荀勖計得留。
units.en: Jia Chong used Xun Xu’s ruse to remain at court.
units.literal: Chong using Xun Xu’s plan obtained stay.

units.zh: 充既為帝所遇，欲專名勢，而庾純、張華、溫顒、向秀、和嶠之徒皆與愷善，楊珧、王恂、華廙等充所親敬，於是朋黨紛然。
units.en: Favored by the emperor, Jia Chong wished to monopolize fame and power, while Yu Chun, Zhang Hua, Wen Yong, Xiang Xiu, He Jiao and their like all befriended Kai, and Yang Yao, Wang Xun, and Hua Yi were those Chong held dear, so factional cliques flared.
units.literal: Chong having been favored by Emperor wished monopolize fame and power—while Yu Chun, Zhang Hua, Wen Yong, Xiang Xiu, He Jiao and their like all befriended Kai—Yang Yao, Wang Xun, Hua Yi and such Chong held dear—thereby faction cliques flared.

units.zh: 帝知之，召充、愷宴於式乾殿，而謂充等曰：「朝廷宜一，大臣當和。」
units.en: The emperor summoned both factions to Shiqian Hall and said: "The court should be one; great ministers should harmonize."
units.literal: Emperor knowing it—summoned Chong and Kai to feast at Shiqian Hall—and said to Chong and others: "Court ought be one—great ministers ought harmonize."

units.zh: 充、愷各拜謝而罷。
units.en: Both sides bowed off and left.
units.literal: Chong and Kai each bowed thanks and ceased.

units.zh: 既而充、愷等以帝已知之而不責，結怨愈深，外相崇重，內甚不平。
units.en: Assured the throne would not punish them, Jia Chong and Ren Kai feigned respect while hating each other more.
units.literal: Thereafter Chong, Kai and others because Emperor already knew yet did not blame—knot of hatred grew deeper—outwardly mutual esteem—innerly very unbalanced.

units.zh: 或為充謀曰：「愷總門下樞要，得與上親接，宜啟令典選，便得漸疏，此一都令史事耳。
units.en: A counselor urged Jia Chong: "Ren Kai controls the privy chancery and has intimate access—memorialize to put him in charge of selection and he will grow distant; that is only a capital clerk's affair.
units.literal: Someone for Chong schemed: "Kai governs privy-chamber pivot—gains close access to superiors—ought memorialize to make him superintend selection—then can gradually grow distant—this is one capital clerk’s affair.

units.zh: 且九流難精，間隙易乘。」
units.en: Moreover the nine grades are hard to master—cracks invite attack."
units.literal: Moreover nine currents hard to master—cracks easy to exploit."

units.zh: 充因稱愷才能，宜在官人之職。
units.en: Jia Chong praised Ren Kai’s fitness for personnel.
units.literal: Chong therefore praised Kai’s talent—ought hold office of ordering men.

units.zh: 帝不之疑，謂充舉得其才。
units.en: Emperor Wu trusted the nomination.
units.literal: Emperor did not suspect—said Chong’s recommendation obtained right talent.

units.zh: 即日以愷為吏部尚書，加奉車都尉。
units.en: Ren Kai became minister of personnel with added military rank.
units.literal: Same day appointed Kai minister of personnel—added commandant of palace carriage.

units.zh: 愷既在尚書，選舉公平，盡心所職，然侍覲轉希。
units.en: He ran fair exams but rarely saw the emperor.
units.literal: Kai already in ministry—selection fair—exhausted heart in duty—yet palace audiences grew rarer.

units.zh: 充與荀勖、馮紞承間浸潤，謂愷豪侈，用御食器。
units.en: Jia Chong, Xun Xu, and Feng Dan whispered that Ren Kai used imperial tableware.
units.literal: Chong with Xun Xu, Feng Dan seizing intervals insinuated—claimed Kai extravagant—used imperial dining vessels.

units.zh: 充遣尚書右僕射、高陽王珪奏愷，遂免官。
units.en: They had Prince Gui impeach him—Ren Kai lost his post.
units.literal: Chong sent vice director of right Prince of Gaoyang Gui memorialize Kai—thereupon dismissed office.

units.zh: 有司收太官宰人檢核，是愷妻齊長公主得賜魏時御器也。
units.en: Investigators found only wedding gifts from Wei—Princess Chang’s old imperial vessels.
units.literal: Responsible offices seized grand provisioner butchers and examined—it was Kai’s wife Princess Chang of Qi granted Wei-era imperial vessels.

units.zh: 愷既免而譭謗益至，帝漸薄之。
units.en: Vindicated yet still smeared, Ren Kai fell from favor.
units.literal: Kai already dismissed yet slander increased—Emperor gradually slighted him.

units.zh: 然山濤明愷為人通敏有智局，舉為河南尹。
units.en: Shan Tao still named him Henan governor.
units.literal: Yet Shan Tao clarified Kai’s person astute with wise capacity—recommended as governor of Henan.

units.zh: 坐賊發不獲，又免官。
units.en: He lost the post when bandits escaped capture.
units.literal: Sat because bandits rose—not captured—again dismissed office.

units.zh: 復遷光祿勳。
units.en: He returned as superintendent of the household.
units.literal: Again promoted superintendent of the household.

units.zh: 愷素有識鑒，加以在公勤恪，甚得朝野稱譽。
units.en: Ren Kai’s discernment and diligence won wide praise.
units.literal: Kai by nature had judgment—added to public diligence scrupulous—greatly won court and wild praise.

units.zh: 而賈充朋黨又諷有司奏愷與立進令劉友交關。
units.en: Jia’s clique tied him to Prefect Liu You.
units.literal: Yet Jia Chong faction again hinted responsible offices memorialize Kai connected with Director of Stand-Fast Advance Liu You.

units.zh: 事下尚書，愷對不伏。
units.en: Ren Kai pleaded innocent before the ministry.
units.literal: Matter sent to ministry—Kai replied not submitting.

units.zh: 尚書杜友、廷尉劉良並忠公士也，知愷為充所抑，欲申理之，故遲留而未斷，以是愷及友、良皆免官。
units.en: Du You and Liu Liang stalled to clear him—all three were cashiered.
units.literal: Minister Du You, commandant Liu Liang both loyal fair gentlemen—knew Kai suppressed by Chong—wished clarify—therefore delayed without deciding—thereby Kai and You and Liang all dismissed office.

units.zh: 愷既失職，乃縱酒耽樂，極滋味以自奉養。
units.en: Out of office he drowned in wine and food.
units.literal: Kai having lost office—thereupon indulged wine and pleasure—extreme flavors to support himself.

units.zh: 初，何劭以公子奢侈，每食必盡四方珍饌，愷乃逾之，一食萬錢，猶云無可下箸處。
units.en: He outspent He Shao’s legendary feasts—ten thousand cash per sitting yet claiming nothing worth eating.
units.literal: Earlier He Shao as noble son extravagant—each meal must exhaust four quarters’ rare delicacies—Kai then surpassed—one meal ten thousand cash—still said nowhere to place chopsticks.

units.zh: 愷時因朝請，帝或慰諭之，愷初無復言，惟泣而已。
units.en: At audiences the emperor consoled him—Ren Kai could only weep.
units.literal: Kai sometimes by court briefing—Emperor occasionally comforted instruct—Kai at first had no further words—only weeping.

units.zh: 後起為太僕，轉太常。
units.en: He returned as grand coachman then minister of ceremonies.
units.literal: Later raised grand coachman—transferred minister of ceremonies.

units.zh: 初，魏舒雖歷位郡守，而未被任遇，愷為侍中，薦舒為散騎常侍。
units.en: Ren Kai once lifted Wei Shu from obscurity to the attendant corps.
units.literal: Earlier Wei Shu though repeatedly prefect—not yet met employment favor—Kai as palace attendant recommended Shu as regular attendant at casual riding.

units.zh: 至是舒為右光祿、開府，領司徒，帝臨軒使愷拜授。
units.en: Now Wei Shu stood above him as minister—Emperor Wu made Ren Kai hand him the seal.
units.literal: At this Shu was right grand messenger—opening office—heading minister of education—Emperor facing portico had Kai perform investiture.

units.zh: 舒雖以弘量寬簡為稱，時以愷有佐世器局，而舒登三公，愷止守散卿，莫不為之憤歎也。
units.en: People resented that Shu surpassed the man who once sponsored him.
units.literal: Shu though by vast capacity broad simplicity praised—men of time thought Kai had aid-the-age vessel—yet Shu ascended Three Dukes—Kai only guarded ordinary minister—none not for him indignant sigh.

units.zh: 愷不得志，竟以憂卒，時年六十一，諡曰元，子罕嗣。
units.en: He died heartsick at sixty-one—canonized Yuan—son Ren Han inherited.
units.literal: Kai unfulfilled in ambition—ended dying of grief—age sixty-one—posthumous title Yuan—son Han succeeded.

units.zh: 子罕
units.en: His son Ren Han
units.literal: Son Han

units.zh: =罕字子倫，幼有門風，才望不及愷，以淑行致稱，為清平佳士。
units.en: Ren Han, styled Zilun, lacked his father’s fame but won praise as a sober gentleman.
units.literal: =Han courtesy name Zilun—had family manner from youth—talent reputation did not reach Kai—by chaste conduct earned praise—was clear fair excellent gentleman.

units.zh: 歷黃門侍郎、散騎常侍、兗州刺史、大鴻臚。
units.en: He rose through the palace to grand herald.
units.literal: Served gentleman attendant at yellow gate—regular attendant at casual riding—inspector of Yanzhou—grand herald.

units.zh: 崔洪
units.en: Cui Hong
units.literal: Cui Hong

units.zh: 崔洪，字良伯，博陵安平人也。
units.en: Cui Hong, styled Liangbo, came from Anping in Boling.
units.literal: Cui Hong, courtesy name Liangbo, was native of Anping in Boling.

units.zh: 高祖寔，著名漢代。
units.en: Ancestor Cui Shi was celebrated under the Han.
units.literal: High ancestor Shi—famed in Han era.

units.zh: 父贊，魏吏部尚書、左僕射，以雅量見稱。
units.en: His father Cui Zan led Wei personnel and was famed for equanimity.
units.literal: Father Zan—Wei minister of personnel, vice director left—praised by spacious capacity.

units.zh: 洪少以清厲顯名，骨鯁不同於物，人之有過，輒面折之，而退無後言。
units.en: He was blunt—scolding faults to one’s face yet silent behind backs.
units.literal: Hong from youth by pure stern showed name—backbone straight different from things—when men had fault—then face rebuke—yet retiring no behind speech.

units.zh: 武帝世，為御史治書。
units.en: Under Emperor Wu he served as legal editorial clerk.
units.literal: Emperor Wu age—was editorial clerk for law.

units.zh: 時長樂馮恢父為弘農太守，愛少子淑，欲以爵傳之。
units.en: Feng Hui’s father planned to disinherit his heir for a younger son.
units.literal: At time Changle Feng Hui’s father was prefect of Hongnong—loved youngest son Shu—wished transmit noble rank to him.

units.zh: 恢父終，服闋，乃還鄉里，結草為廬，陽喑不能言，淑得襲爵。
units.en: When Hui’s father died and mourning was completed, Hui returned to his village, built a grass hut, and feigned muteness so that Shu obtained the inherited noble rank.
units.literal: After father ended mourning—returned village—knotted grass into hut—feigned dumb unable speak—Shu obtained inherited noble.

units.zh: 恢始仕為博士祭酒，散騎常侍翟嬰薦恢高行邁俗，侔繼古烈。
units.en: Feng Hui won praise as a rustic sage—Zhai Ying hailed him.
units.literal: Hui first took office as libationer of erudites—regular attendant Zhai Ying recommended Hui high conduct surpassing custom—match ancient stalwarts.

units.zh: 洪奏恢不敦儒素，令學生番直左右，雖有讓侯微善，不得稱無倫輩，嬰為浮華之目。
units.en: Cui Hong argued Feng Hui’s stunt disgraced scholarship—Zhai Ying’s praise was mere fashion.
units.literal: Hong memorialized Hui did not cultivate Confucian plainness—ordered students rotate duty at side—though had yielding noble slight goodness—cannot be called peerless—Ying gave florid label.

units.zh: 遂免嬰官，朝廷憚之。
units.en: Zhai Ying fell—officials dreaded Cui Hong.
units.literal: Thereupon dismissed Ying office—court feared him.

units.zh: 尋為尚書左丞，時人為之語曰：「叢生棘刺，來自博陵。
units.en: Soon vice minister spawned a rhyme: "Thorns from Boling—
units.literal: Soon minister of the left—men of time made saying: "Thorns in thickets—come from Boling.

units.zh: 在南為鷂，在北為鷹。」
units.en: south as goshawk—north as eagle."
units.literal: In south is goshawk—in north is eagle."

units.zh: 選吏部尚書，舉用甄明，門無私謁。
units.en: As minister of personnel he barred private pleading.
units.literal: Selected minister of personnel—promotions clear—gate without private visits.

units.zh: 薦雍州刺史郤詵代己為左丞。
units.en: He named Xi Shen of Yongzhou to succeed him as vice minister.
units.literal: Recommended Yongzhou inspector Xi Shen replace himself as minister of left.

units.zh: 詵後糾洪，洪謂人曰：「我舉郤丞而還奏我，是挽弩自射也。」
units.en: Xi Shen later impeached him; Cui Hong told others: "I recommended Vice-director Xi yet he memorializes against me—it is like drawing a crossbow to shoot oneself."
units.literal: Shen later impeached Hong—Hong told men: "I raised Vice-director Xi yet he memorializes me—this draws crossbow to shoot self."

units.zh: 詵聞曰：「昔趙宣子任韓厥為司馬，以軍法戮宣子之僕。
units.en: Xi Shen heard and said: "Of old Zhao Dun appointed Han Jue marshal, and by military law Han executed Dun's groom.
units.literal: Shen hearing said: "Of old Zhao Dun appointed Han Jue as marshal—by military law executed Dun’s groom.

units.zh: 宣子謂諸大夫曰：'可賀我矣，我選厥也任其事。
units.en: Zhao Dun rejoiced at Han Jue’s integrity.
units.literal: Dun told assembled grandees: 'Congratulate me—I chose Jue for ability.

units.zh: '崔侯為國舉才，我以才見舉，惟官是視，各明至公，何故私言乃至此！」
units.en: Lord Cui raised talent for the state—I was raised for talent—we look only to office and each uphold utmost fairness—why such private talk!"
units.literal: Lord Cui raised talent for state—I raised by talent—only office viewed—each illuminates utmost fairness—why private words reach here!"

units.zh: 洪聞其言而重之。
units.en: Cui Hong respected the reply.
units.literal: Hong hearing his words esteemed him.

units.zh: 洪口不言貨財，手不執珠玉。
units.en: He neither hoarded coin nor fingered gems.
units.literal: Hong mouth did not speak goods wealth—hand did not hold pearls jade.

units.zh: 汝南王亮常晏公卿，以琉璃鐘行酒。
units.en: Prince Liang feasted ministers with a glass wine bowl.
units.literal: Prince of Runan Liang often banqueted dukes and ministers—used glass bell-cup to pass wine.

units.zh: 酒及洪，洪不執。
units.en: Cui Hong refused the cup.
units.literal: Wine reached Hong—Hong did not take.

units.zh: 亮問其故，對曰：「慮有執玉不趨之義故爾」。
units.en: When Prince Liang asked why, he replied: "I feared the ritual meaning of holding jade without hurrying."
units.literal: Liang asked cause—replied: "Fearing meaning of holding jade not hurry—therefore thus."

units.zh: 然實乖其常性，故為詭說。
units.en: He invented etiquette to mask stinginess.
units.literal: Yet truly violated his constant nature—therefore made crafty explanation.

units.zh: 楊駿誅，洪與都水使者王佑親，坐見黜。
units.en: After Yang Jun fell—his tie to Wang You cost him rank.
units.literal: Yang Jun executed—Hong with commissioner of waters Wang You intimate—sat and saw demotion.

units.zh: 後為大司農，卒於官。
units.en: He ended as minister of agriculture.
units.literal: Later minister of agriculture—died in office.

units.zh: 子廓
units.en: His son Cui Kuo
units.literal: Son Kuo

units.zh: =子廓，散騎侍郎，亦以正直稱。
units.en: Cui Kuo served as attendant—praised like his father.
units.literal: =Kuo, attendant at casual riding—also by upright straight praised.

units.zh: 郭奕
units.en: Guo Yi
units.literal: Guo Yi

units.zh: 郭奕，字大業，太原陽曲人也。
units.en: Guo Yi, styled Daye, came from Yangqu in Taiyuan.
units.literal: Guo Yi, courtesy name Daye, native of Yangqu in Taiyuan.

units.zh: 少有重名，山濤稱其高簡有雅量。
units.en: Shan Tao admired his calm restraint.
units.literal: From youth had heavy fame—Shan Tao praised his lofty spare spacious capacity.

units.zh: 初為野王令，羊祜常過之，奕歎曰：「羊叔子何必減郭大業！」
units.en: As magistrate of Yewang, when Yang Hu often visited, Guo Yi sighed: "Uncle Yangzi need not rank below Guo Daye!"
units.literal: First he was magistrate of Yewang; Yang Hu often visited; Yi sighed: "Why should Uncle Shuzi rank below Guo Daye!"

units.zh: 少選復往，又歎曰：「羊叔子去人遠矣。」
units.en: Shortly he went again and sighed: "Uncle Yangzi stands far above ordinary men."
units.literal: Shortly again went—again sighed: "Uncle Yangzi far surpasses men."

units.zh: 遂送祜出界數百里，坐此免官。
units.en: He escorted Yang Hu hundreds of li past his border—lost his post for it.
units.literal: Then escorted Hu beyond boundary several hundred li—sat because dismissed office.

units.zh: 咸熙末，為文帝相國主薄。
units.en: Late in Xianxi he served as chief clerk to Emperor Wen, the minister of state.
units.literal: Late Xianxi—became Emperor Wen’s minister-of-state chief clerk.

units.zh: 時鍾會反于蜀，荀勖即會之從甥，少長會家，勖為文帝掾，奕啟出之。
units.en: When Zhong Hui rebelled in Shu, Guo Yi urged removing Xun Xu—Hui’s nephew, raised in Hui’s house and then an aide of Emperor Wen—from that staff.
units.literal: At time Zhong Hui rebelled in Shu—Xun Xu was Hui’s nephew—raised from youth in Hui household—Xu was Prince Wen aide—Yi memorialize remove him.

units.zh: 帝雖不用，然知其雅正。
units.en: Prince Zhao noted his integrity despite rejecting the memo.
units.literal: Emperor though did not use—yet knew his upright correctness.

units.zh: 武帝踐阼，初建東宮，以奕及鄭默並為中庶子。
units.en: Emperor Wu named him heir adjunct with Zheng Mo.
units.literal: Emperor Wu mounting throne—first established eastern palace—made Yi and Zheng Mo both heir-adjuncts.

units.zh: 遷右衛率、驍騎將軍，封平陵男。
units.en: He rose to guard colonel and cavalry general—Baron of Pingling.
units.literal: Promoted colonel of right guard—general Who Gallops Cavalry—enfeoffed Baron of Pingling.

units.zh: 咸寧初，遷雍州刺史、鷹揚將軍，尋假赤幢曲蓋、鼓吹。
units.en: Early Xianning he governed Yongzhou with general’s banners and band.
units.literal: Early Xianning—promoted inspector of Yongzhou—general Who Raises Hawk—soon borrowed crimson canopy curved parasol—military band.

units.zh: 奕有寡姊，隨奕之官，姊下僮僕多有奸犯，而為人所糾。
units.en: His widowed sister’s servants broke laws—others impeached him.
units.literal: Yi had widowed elder sister—followed Yi to office—sister’s servants many wicked offenders—yet impeached by others.

units.zh: 奕省按畢，曰：「大丈夫豈當以老姊求名？」
units.en: After his review he said: "Should a great man trade on an aged sister to seek reputation?"
units.literal: Yi examined finished—said: "Great man how should use old sister seek fame?"

units.zh: 遂遣而不問。
units.en: He released the matter—preserving family peace.
units.literal: Then sent away without questioning.

units.zh: 時亭長李含有俊才，而門寒為豪族所排，奕用為別駕，含後果有名位，時以奕為知人。
units.en: He promoted clerk Li Han despite mighty families’ spite—later hailed as a judge of talent.
units.literal: At time precinct chief Li Han had splendid talent—yet gate humble pressed by powerful clan—Yi employed as aide—Han afterward indeed won name position—time took Yi as knowing men.

units.zh: 太康中，徵為尚書。
units.en: Taikang recalled him to the ministry.
units.literal: Taikang period—summoned minister of state affairs.

units.zh: 奕有重名，當世朝臣皆出其下。
units.en: Peers ranked beneath his stature.
units.literal: Yi had heavy fame—contemporary court ministers all below him.

units.zh: 時帝委任楊駿，奕表駿小器，不可任以社稷。
units.en: He warned that Yang Jun was too small for state duty.
units.literal: At time Emperor entrusted Yang Jun—Yi memorialized Jun petty vessel—cannot entrust altars of soil and grain.

units.zh: 帝不聽，駿後果誅。
units.en: Wu ignored him—Yang Jun soon died.
units.literal: Emperor did not listen—Jun afterward indeed executed.

units.zh: 及奕疾病，詔賜錢二十萬，日給酒米。
units.en: Illness brought imperial stipends of cash and grain.
units.literal: When Yi fell ill—edict granted cash two hundred thousand—daily supplied wine grain.

units.zh: 太康八年卒，太常上諡為景。
units.en: In the eighth year of Taikang, the ministry first proposed “Jing.”
units.literal: In the eighth year of Taikang, Died—minister of ceremonies upward memorial posthumous title Jing.

units.zh: 有司議以貴賤不同號，諡與景皇同，不可，請諡曰穆。
units.en: Court noted “Jing” matched Emperor Jing—requested “Mu” instead.
units.literal: Responsible offices debated noble humble different titles—posthumous same as Emperor Jing—not permissible—request posthumous Mu.

units.zh: 詔曰：「諡所以旌德表行，按諡法一德不懈為簡。
units.en: The throne cited the canon “steady”—Jian.
units.literal: Edict said: "Posthumous title thereby banners virtue displays conduct—examining posthumous law one virtue unceasing is Jian.

units.zh: 奕忠毅清直，立德不渝。」
units.en: Guo Yi was loyal, resolute, pure, and upright—his established virtue never wavered."
units.literal: Yi loyal resolute pure straight—established virtue not altered."

units.zh: 於是遂賜諡曰簡。
units.en: He was canonized “Jian.”
units.literal: Thereupon granted posthumous title Jian.

units.zh: 侯史光
units.en: Houshi Guang
units.literal: Houshi Guang

units.zh: 侯史光，字孝明，東萊掖人也。
units.en: Houshi Guang, styled Xiaoming, came from Ye in Donglai.
units.literal: Houshi Guang, courtesy name Xiaoming, native of Ye in Donglai.

units.zh: 幼有才悟，受學于同縣劉夏。
units.en: He studied under Liu Xia in his county.
units.literal: From youth had talent perception—received learning from same county Liu Xia.

units.zh: 舉孝廉，州辟別駕。
units.en: Recommended filial and honest—provincial aide.
units.literal: Nominated filial incorrupt—province summoned aide.

units.zh: 咸熙初，為洛陽典農中郎將，封關中侯。
units.en: Early Xianxi he commanded Luoyang farming troops—Marquis Within the Pass.
units.literal: Early Xianxi—Luoyang agrarian colonel—enfeoffed marquis within Guan.

units.zh: 泰始初，拜散騎常侍，尋兼侍中。
units.en: Taishi brought him to the attendant corps and palace.
units.literal: Taishi beginning—appointed regular attendant at casual riding—soon concurrently palace attendant.

units.zh: 與皇甫陶、荀暠持節循省風俗，及還，奏事稱旨，轉城門校尉，進爵臨海侯。
units.en: With Huangfu Tao and Xun Gao he held credentials, toured inspecting customs, and on return, his report meeting with approval, was transferred to colonel of the city gates and advanced to Marquis of Linhai.
units.literal: With Huangfu Tao, Xun Gao holding credentials toured inspected customs—when returned—memorialized matters fitting intent—transferred colonel of City Gates—advanced noble rank marquis of Linhai.

units.zh: 其年詔曰：「光忠亮篤素，有居正執義之心，歷職內外，恪勤在公，其以光為御史中丞。
units.en: That year an edict said: "Guang is loyal, bright, and plain in devotion, with a heart that upholds rectitude; serving inside and outside with scrupulous diligence—let Guang be imperial secretary.
units.literal: That year edict said: "Guang loyal bright devoted plain—has dwell upright hold righteousness heart—served inner outer offices—scrupulous diligent in public—make Guang palace secretary.

units.zh: 雖屈其列校之位，亦所以伸其司直之才。」
units.en: Though this bends his colonel's rank, it extends his censorial talent."
units.literal: Though bent his ranked-colonel position—also thereby extend his straightening talent."

units.zh: 光在職寬而不縱。
units.en: As secretary he was firm but fair.
units.literal: Guang in office lenient yet not lax.

units.zh: 太保王祥久疾廢朝，光奏請免之，詔優祥而寢光奏。
units.en: He memorialized to dismiss Grand Guardian Wang Xiang for long illness; an edict favored Xiang and shelved Guang’s memorial.
units.literal: Grand Tutor Wang Xiang long ill ceased court—Guang memorialized request dismiss—edict favored Xiang yet shelved Guang memorial.

units.zh: 後遷少府，卒官，詔賜朝服一具、衣一襲、錢三十萬、布百匹。
units.en: Promoted privy-treasury minister, he died in office; the court sent burial robes, thirty thousand cash, and a hundred bolts of cloth.
units.literal: Later promoted minister of the privy purse—died in office—edict gifted court robes one set—garments one suit—cash thirty thousand—cloth one hundred bolts.

units.zh: 及葬，又詔曰：「光厲志守約，有清忠之節。
units.en: At burial another edict said: "Guang hardened his will and kept restraint, with pure loyal bearing.
units.literal: When buried—again edict said: "Guang hardened will kept restraint—had pure loyal bearing.

units.zh: 家極貧儉，其賜錢五十萬。」
units.en: His household is extremely poor and frugal—grant fifty thousand cash."
units.literal: House extremely poor frugal—grant cash fifty thousand."

units.zh: 光儒學博古，歷官著績，文筆奏議皆有條理。
units.en: Houshi Guang mastered classical lore; his memorials were models of clarity.
units.literal: Guang Confucian learning broad antiquity—each office showed merit—literary brush memorials all had order.

units.zh: 長子玄嗣，官至玄菟太守。
units.en: Son Houshi Xuan rose to Xuantu prefect.
units.literal: Eldest son Xuan succeeded—office reached prefect of Xuantu.

units.zh: 卒，子施嗣，東莞太守。
units.en: He died; son Houshi Shi became Dongguan prefect.
units.literal: Died—son Shi succeeded—prefect of Dongguan.

units.zh: 何攀
units.en: He Pan
units.literal: He Pan

units.zh: 何攀，字惠興，蜀郡郫人也。
units.en: He Pan, styled Huixing, came from Pi in Shu.
units.literal: He Pan, courtesy name Huixing, native of Pi in Shu commandery.

units.zh: 仕州為主薄。
units.en: He began as a provincial chief clerk.
units.literal: Served province as chief clerk.

units.zh: 屬刺史皇甫晏為牙門張弘所害，誣以大逆。
units.en: Inspector Huangfu Yan was murdered by Zhang Hong and smeared as a traitor.
units.literal: When Inspector Huangfu Yan was harmed by camp gate Zhang Hong—slandered with great treason.

units.zh: 時攀適丁母喪，遂詣梁州拜表，證晏不反，故晏冤理得申。
units.en: Though mourning his mother, he rode to Liangzhou and cleared Huangfu Yan’s name.
units.literal: At time Pan happened mourning mother—thereupon went to Liangzhou submitting memorial—proved Yan did not rebel—therefore Yan’s wrong managed to clear.

units.zh: 王濬為益州，辟為別駕。
units.en: Wang Jun made him provincial aide in Yi.
units.literal: Wang Jun as Yi province—summoned as aide.

units.zh: 濬謀伐吳，遣攀奉表詣台，口陳事機，詔再引見，乃令張華與攀籌量進時討之宜。
units.en: He Pan carried Wang Jun’s Wu campaign memorial to Luoyang and planned timing with Zhang Hua.
units.literal: Jun schemed attacking Wu—sent Pan bearing memorial to court—orally stated opportunity—edict twice summoned audience—ordered Zhang Hua with Pan deliberate advancing timing of attack fitness.

units.zh: 濬兼遣攀過羊祜，面陳伐吳之策。
units.en: He also briefed Yang Hu in person on the Wu invasion.
units.literal: Jun also sent Pan visit Yang Hu—face to face state attacking Wu strategies.

units.zh: 攀善於將命，帝善之，詔攀參濬軍事。
units.en: His diplomacy pleased Emperor Wu, who attached him to Wang Jun’s staff.
units.literal: Pan good at carrying orders—Emperor praised—ordered Pan assist Jun military affairs.

units.zh: 及孫皓降于濬，而王渾恚於後機，欲攻濬，攀勸濬送皓與渾，由是事解。
units.en: When Wang Hun nearly attacked Wang Jun over Sun Hao’s surrender, He Pan urged handing the captive to Hun to prevent civil bloodshed.
units.literal: When Sun Hao surrendered to Jun—yet Wang Hun angry at late timing—wished attack Jun—Pan urged Jun deliver Hao to Hun—thereby matter resolved.

units.zh: 以攀為濬輔國司馬，封關內侯。
units.en: Wang Jun named him auxiliary marshal—Marquis Within the Pass.
units.literal: Made Pan Jun aids-state marshal—enfeoffed marquis within Guan.

units.zh: 轉滎陽令，上便宜十事，甚得名稱。
units.en: As Xingyang magistrate he offered ten reform memos and won fame.
units.literal: Transferred Xingyang magistrate—submitted convenient matters ten items—greatly earned reputation.

units.zh: 除廷尉平。
units.en: He became a justice assessor.
units.literal: Appointed commandant-ping of justice.

units.zh: 時廷尉卿諸葛沖以攀蜀士，輕之，及共斷疑獄，沖始嘆服。
units.en: Zhuge Chong sneered at his Shu origins until joint trials proved his genius.
units.literal: At time commandant of justice Zhuge Chong because Pan Shu gentleman—slighted him—when together judged doubtful lawsuits—Chong then sighed admiration.

units.zh: 遷宣城太守，不行，轉散騎侍郎。
units.en: He declined Xuancheng but joined the attendant corps.
units.literal: Promoted prefect of Xuancheng—did not go—transferred regular attendant at casual riding.

units.zh: 楊駿執政，多樹親屬，大開封嘗，欲以恩澤自衛。
units.en: Regent Yang Jun stuffed offices with kin and blanketed them with patents.
units.literal: Yang Jun holding power—planted many kin—greatly opened investitures rewards—wished by grace shield self.

units.zh: 攀以為非，乃與石崇共立議奏之。
units.en: He Pan and Shi Chong jointly condemned the policy.
units.literal: Pan thought not right—thereupon with Shi Chong jointly stood memorial submitting.

units.zh: 語在崇傳。
units.en: (See the biography of Shi Chong.)
units.literal: Language is in Chong biography.

units.zh: 帝不納。
units.en: The emperor ignored them.
units.literal: Emperor did not accept.

units.zh: 以豫誅駿功，封西城侯，邑萬戶，賜絹萬匹，弟逢平卿侯，兄子逵關中侯。
units.en: For merit in executing Yang Jun he was enfeoffed Marquis of Xicheng with ten thousand households and ten thousand bolts of silk; his younger brother Feng became Marquis of Pingqing and his elder brother’s son Kui Marquis Within the Pass.
units.literal: By merit participating executing Jun—enfeoffed marquis of Xicheng—ten thousand households—gift silk ten thousand bolts—younger brother Feng Pingqing marquis—elder brother’s son Kui marquis within Guan.

units.zh: 攀固讓所封戶及絹之半，餘所受者分給中外宗親，略不入己。
units.en: He refused half the silk and fiefs—sharing the rest with kin—keeping nothing.
units.literal: Pan firmly declined half of granted households and silk—remainder received distributed inside outside kin—almost none entered self.

units.zh: 遷翊軍校尉，頃之，出為東羌校尉。
units.en: He became aide colonel then Eastern Qiang colonel.
units.literal: Promoted colonel Who Aids Army—shortly—went out colonel of Eastern Qiang.

units.zh: 徵為揚州刺史，在任三年，遷大司農。
units.en: After three years as Yangzhou inspector he headed the ministry of agriculture.
units.literal: Summoned inspector of Yang province—in office three years—promoted minister of agriculture.

units.zh: 轉兗州刺史，加鷹揚將軍，固讓不就。
units.en: He refused Yanzhou despite general’s banners.
units.literal: Transferred inspector of Yanzhou—added general Who Raises Hawk—firmly declined did not take.

units.zh: 太常成粲、左將軍卞粹勸攀蒞職，中詔又加切厲，攀竟稱疾不起。
units.en: Minister of Ceremonies Cheng Can and General of the Left Bian Cui urged him to take the post; an inner edict grew stern, but Pan claimed illness and would not rise.
units.literal: Minister of ceremonies Cheng Can—general left Bian Cui urged Pan take office—inner edict again stern—Pan ultimately claimed illness did not rise.

units.zh: 及趙王倫篡位，遣使召攀，更稱疾篤。
units.en: Prince Lun’s summons met another refusal—grave illness.
units.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun usurped—sent envoy summon Pan—again claimed grave illness.

units.zh: 倫怒，將誅之，攀不得已，扶疾赴召。
units.en: Lun threatened death—He Pan dragged himself to Luoyang.
units.literal: Lun angry—would execute—Pan had no choice—supported illness answered summons.

units.zh: 卒于洛陽，時年五十八。
units.en: He died there at fifty-eight.
units.literal: Died in Luoyang—age fifty-eight.

units.zh: 攀居心平允，蒞官整肅，愛樂人物，敦儒貴才。
units.en: Fair-minded and orderly in office, he honored scholars and talent.
units.literal: Pan dwelling mind fair—holding office stern—loved delighted men—esteemed Confucian prized talent.

units.zh: 為梁、益二州中正，引致遺滯。
units.en: As Liang-Yi rectifier he recalled unjustly blocked men.
units.literal: As grand rectifier for Liang and Yi provinces—drew in stranded men.

units.zh: 巴西陳壽、閻乂、犍為費立皆西州名士，並被鄉閭所謗，清議十餘年。
units.en: Chen Shou and western scholars suffered decade-long village boycotts.
units.literal: Baixi Chen Shou—Yan Yi—Fei Li of Qianwei—all western province famed gentlemen—together slandered by villages—pure discussion over ten years.

units.zh: 攀申明曲直，咸免冤濫。
units.en: He Pan reversed their verdicts—clearing injustice.
units.literal: Pan clarified crooked straight—all spared wrongful overflow.

units.zh: 攀雖居顯職，家甚貧素，無妾媵伎樂，惟以周窮濟乏為事。
units.en: Despite high rank he stayed poor—no concubines or musicians—only charity.
units.literal: Pan though occupied eminent office—house very poor plain—no concubines singing girls—only took relieving poverty aiding want as task.

units.zh: 子璋嗣，亦有父風。
units.en: Son He Zhang inherited his integrity.
units.literal: Son Zhang succeeded—also had father manner.

units.zh: 史評
units.en: Historians’ appraisal
units.literal: Historians’ appraisal

units.zh: 史臣曰：幽厲不君，上德猶懷進善；
units.en: Even under tyrants worthies still hoped to counsel virtue;
units.literal: Historians say: You and Li did not lord—high virtue still cherished advancing goodness;

units.zh: 共驩在位，大聖之所不堪。
units.en: Gong and Huan in power were more than even a great sage could endure;
units.literal: Gong Huan on throne—great sage cannot endure.

units.zh: 況乎志士仁人，甯求苟合！
units.en: how much less would principled men trim truth for favor!
units.literal: How much more intent gentlemen and benevolent men—would they seek careless conformity!

units.zh: 懷其寵秩，所以系其存亡者也。
units.en: Rank and stipend bind ministers’ survival—
units.literal: Cherishing their favor and salary—thereby ties their survival.

units.zh: 雖復自口銷金，投光撫劍，馳書北闕，敗車猶踐，而諫主不易，譏臣實難。
units.en: yet even facing ruin remonstrating proves harder than flattering—truth cuts both ways.
units.literal: Though again mouths melt metal—cast aside brilliance grasp sword—gallop memorial northern gate—broken cart still tread—yet remonstrating lord not easy—mocking ministers truly hard.

units.zh: 劉毅一遇寬容，任和兩遭膚受，詳觀餘烈，亦各其心焉。
units.en: Liu Yi won rare patience—Ren Kai and He Jiao suffered credulous courts—each followed conscience nonetheless.
units.literal: Liu Yi once met tolerance—Ren and He twice suffered shallow belief—closely observing remaining deeds—each also their hearts.

units.zh: 若夫武陔懷魏臣之志，崔洪愛郤詵之道，長升勸王彌之尊，何攀從趙倫之命，君子之人，觀乎臨事者也。
units.en: Wu Gai kept Wei-minister resolve; Cui Hong loved Xi Shen's way; Changsheng urged honor for Wang Mi; He Pan obeyed Zhao Lun's order—a gentleman is seen in the crisis.
units.literal: As for Wu Gai cherishing Wei minister resolve—Cui Hong loving Xi Shen’s way—Changsheng urging Wang Mi’s honor—He Pan obeying Zhao Lun’s order—gentleman quality—observe them at crisis.

units.zh: 贊曰：仲雄初令，忠謇揚庭。
units.en: Verse: Liu Yi’s early zeal shook the court—
units.literal: Praise says: Zhongxiong first command—loyal blunt raised court.

units.zh: 身方諸葛，帝擬桓、靈。
units.en: likened to stern ministers—yet matched with doomed Han emperors;
units.literal: Body compared Zhuge—Emperor likened Huan Ling.

units.zh: 大業非楊，元褒誚賈。
units.en: Daye refused Yang Jun’s tide—Ren Kai mocked Jia Chong;
units.literal: Daye rejected Yang—Yuanbao mocked Jia.

units.zh: 和氏條暢，堪施大廈。
units.en: He Jiao stood tall as ridge timber;
units.literal: He clan lithe—fit to roof great hall.

units.zh: 崔門不謁，聲飛朝野。
units.en: Cui Hong barred favor-seekers yet fame soared;
units.literal: Cui gate unvisited—voice flies court wild.

units.zh: 侯史、武陔，輔佐之才。
units.en: Houshi Guang and Wu Gai served as fine assistants;
units.literal: Houshi and Wu Gai—aiding talents.

units.zh: 何攀平允，冤濫多回。
units.en: He Pan’s fairness redeemed many wrongs.
units.literal: He Pan fair—wrongful overflow much turned.
